attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses this conclusion in his own words.

semantics.note: The rhetorical reference to innocence expresses a retrospective conclusion about candor. In context, it disputes the absence of legitimate grounds for questioning Altman, rather than asserting legal guilt.

contract.note: The contract grounds its reading in Marcus’s explanation of the disputed position. Legitimate candor concerns do not require proving every allegation or showing dismissal was necessary.

evidence.note: Toner supplies firsthand allegations of withheld and inaccurate information relevant to board oversight. These support legitimate concerns, although the interview does not independently verify her allegations.

Earlier reporting describes specific alleged misrepresentations of directors’ positions. It supports the candor concerns while including a denial of manipulation; unnamed sources may overlap with Toner.

Document-based reporting identifies Altman’s signatures on provisions he said he did not know about. This supports grounds for questioning candor, but does not establish that his denial was knowingly false.

This company disclosure reports confidence in leadership and a review finding that removal was not mandated. It does not establish that the board lacked legitimate candor concerns or resolve the specific allegations.

reviews.rationale: Toner’s firsthand account, earlier reporting on representations to directors, and document-based reporting supply substantive grounds for questioning candor under the contract. The denial and company review qualify the evidence but do not negate those grounds. This finding does not establish every alleged lie or justify dismissal.
